title: Oxygen loss and carbon gain came with a 0.075 pH fall on P02 density 26.5 at 180-160 W in 2004-2022
abstract: Does the recent North Pacific oxygen loss have a carbon and acidification signal? We compare common flag-2 bottle measurements on P02 sigma0 26.5 in 2004, 2013 and 2022. In eight matched bins at 180-160 W, oxygen fell by 15.34 micromol/kg and dissolved inorganic carbon rose by 23.42 from 2004 to 2022. Total-scale pH calculated from carbon and alkalinity fell by 0.0746 at fixed temperature, salinity and pressure (conditional spatial interval -0.0781 to -0.0700); in-situ pH fell by 0.0719. With C:N:O=117:16:170, an AOU-based organic process gives 49.7% of the chemical pH fall. Its spatial interval is 40.6-56.0%, but assumed independent calibration bounds widen the point range to 28.6-95.5%. The process share is therefore much less secure than the total pH fall. The envelope of spatial intervals across calibration corners permits a 100% share. Measured pH gives a 2013-2022 change of -0.0304 in six central bins, close to -0.0297 from carbon and alkalinity. The strict interpolation check has too few central bins. An eastern mean aragonite threshold crossing is not resolved by its spatial interval. This joint chemical target extends the oxygen and nutrient tests through 2022. It does not identify local respiration, anthropogenic carbon or an outcrop cause. Sparse sections, shared alkalinity, source-water changes and unmeasured calibration errors limit attribution. Code, aggregate evidence, exact input hashes and an external-data retrieval recipe are supplied.

display.caption: Joint oxygen and carbon evidence at density 26.5. Upper panels use three-year common support. Lower panels use endpoint support. Intervals are conditional spatial intervals; grey ranges are assumed calibration corners.
Measured pH supports the recent carbonate change. The eastern mean saturation threshold is uncertain. The oxygen-equivalent removal is a conditional chemical calculation.
